name: Supplier performance
headline: Supplier K +8% cost notice — should-cost says +2.9%

impact.label: Annual cost
impact.note: across all four decisions, at current volume

data.ackBody: Lead-time changes add $18K of safety stock across the affected categories. The buy plan cannot absorb that silently — Planner sees it here, before anything is agreed with a supplier.

suppliers.name: Kessler Metalworks
suppliers.context: Asked for 8% against a 2.9% should-cost move, while sitting two quarters below the Tier 1 OTD floor. Four SKUs are single-source and $374K of their POs are in flight.
suppliers.planTitle: Counter at +3.0% with an 18-month volume commitment
suppliers.planBody: Open with the should-cost build-up, not with a number. Anchor at +2.9% index-linked, settle at +3.0% in exchange for volume they have not had committed before, and put the OTD recovery plan in the same letter so the two conversations cannot be separated.

__raw.name: Kessler Metalworks
__raw.context: Asked for 8% against a 2.9% should-cost move, while sitting two quarters below the Tier 1 OTD floor. Four SKUs are single-source and $374K of their POs are in flight.

negotiate.title: Counter at +3.0% with an 18-month volume commitment
negotiate.body: Open with the should-cost build-up, not with a number. Anchor at +2.9% index-linked, settle at +3.0% in exchange for volume they have not had committed before, and put the OTD recovery plan in the same letter so the two conversations cannot be separated.

dual.title: Dual-source 40% of volume, hold K at 60%
dual.body: Qualify a second source on the four single-source SKUs and shift 40% of volume. It removes the concentration that produced this notice, but it costs 14 weeks, a safety-stock build, and K will read it as a shot across the bow — which may be the point.

exit.title: Exit Kessler over 14 weeks, honouring all open POs
exit.body: Move all four SKUs to Nanjing at −1.8%. The unit price is better and the concentration risk goes away, but we lose 187 days of contract, absorb a 7-day lead-time increase and a $58K safety-stock build, and give up a supplier whose defect rate is the second-best in the base.

accept.title: Accept +8.0% and log why
accept.body: Logged rationale: "Accepted above should-cost to preserve delivery reliability into Q4 peak with no qualified alternate in place. Revisit at the Mar 31 renewal with the index-linked clause as the primary ask." Costs $70.4K a year and concedes the pattern for the next notice.

suppliers.name: Meridian Filtration
suppliers.context: No price issue — they run below should-cost. Delivery is the problem: 89.2% OTD against a 93% floor, a 61-hour response time, and two stockouts on the filter 3-pack traced to late inbound.
suppliers.planBody: Split the volume rather than replace it. Aquatek quotes +0.9% at a shorter lead time and holds the same certifications, so 50% of the cartridge volume stops depending on a supplier that has missed four quarters running. Meridian keeps the rest and a reason to fix it.

__raw.name: Meridian Filtration
__raw.context: No price issue — they run below should-cost. Delivery is the problem: 89.2% OTD against a 93% floor, a 61-hour response time, and two stockouts on the filter 3-pack traced to late inbound.

negotiate.title: OTD recovery plan with a 90-day review
negotiate.body: Written recovery plan with weekly delivery reporting and a 93% OTD commitment inside 90 days. Cheapest option and it keeps a supplier whose price discipline is good, but we carry interim safety stock and we have run this play with them once already.

dual.title: Dual-source 50% to Aquatek
dual.body: Split the volume rather than replace it. Aquatek quotes +0.9% at a shorter lead time and holds the same certifications, so 50% of the cartridge volume stops depending on a supplier that has missed four quarters running. Meridian keeps the rest and a reason to fix it.

exit.title: Replace Meridian entirely
exit.body: Move all cartridge and pitcher volume to Aquatek. Simplifies the supply base but concentrates a category on a supplier we have never run at full volume, and the stockout risk during transition sits on our highest-repeat SKU.

accept.title: Accept current performance and log why
accept.body: Logged rationale: "No action this quarter; qualification capacity committed to Kessler alternates. Accepting an estimated $14K of stockout cost and revisiting in January." Honest, and cheaper than pretending we have the bandwidth for both.

suppliers.name: Verdant Woodcraft
suppliers.context: Defect rate 640 PPM above the Tier 3 ceiling and rising for six quarters. Returns on the affected SKUs run 9.2% against a 4% norm — the unit-price discount is smaller than what the defects cost us.
suppliers.planTitle: Replace with Alder & Co in 6 weeks
suppliers.planBody: No tooling, no certification, six weeks to qualify. Unit price rises 5.8% and the returns saving is $21K a year, so the switch pays for itself twice over. This is the cheapest supplier in the base to replace and the one with the clearest reason to.

__raw.name: Verdant Woodcraft
__raw.context: Defect rate 640 PPM above the Tier 3 ceiling and rising for six quarters. Returns on the affected SKUs run 9.2% against a 4% norm — the unit-price discount is smaller than what the defects cost us.

negotiate.title: CAPA on splitting and finish defects
negotiate.body: Corrective action on the two defect modes with an 8-week verification window and a chargeback for the return cost on affected lots. Keeps the price, but six quarters of decline is a pattern rather than an incident.

dual.title: Split volume with Alder & Co
dual.body: Half the volume to a better-finish supplier while Verdant works its CAPA. Costs more per unit and keeps two relationships alive for a Tier 3 category that does not really justify either.

exit.title: Replace with Alder & Co in 6 weeks
exit.body: No tooling, no certification, six weeks to qualify. Unit price rises 5.8% and the returns saving is $21K a year, so the switch pays for itself twice over. This is the cheapest supplier in the base to replace and the one with the clearest reason to.

accept.title: Accept the defect rate and log why
accept.body: Logged rationale: "Tier 3 spend, no capacity to run a third transition this quarter." Defensible only if the returns cost is written down next to it: $21K a year, larger than the price advantage.

suppliers.name: Tsuyo Blades
suppliers.context: Performance is fine and pricing tracks should-cost almost exactly. The only thing on the table is terms — Net 30 against a Net 45 target, worth $19K of working capital a year at current spend.
suppliers.planBody: No price conversation at all. Ask for 15 days of terms in exchange for a two-year renewal and consolidated monthly ordering, which reduces their admin as much as it helps our cash. Walk-away is simply staying where we are.

__raw.name: Tsuyo Blades
__raw.context: Performance is fine and pricing tracks should-cost almost exactly. The only thing on the table is terms — Net 30 against a Net 45 target, worth $19K of working capital a year at current spend.

negotiate.title: Terms-only ask: Net 30 → Net 45
negotiate.body: No price conversation at all. Ask for 15 days of terms in exchange for a two-year renewal and consolidated monthly ordering, which reduces their admin as much as it helps our cash. Walk-away is simply staying where we are.

dual.title: Dual-source for leverage
dual.body: Qualifying Seki would give us a second knife source, but it costs 12 weeks and $31K to gain leverage in a negotiation about 15 days of payment terms. The cost of the tool exceeds the value of the win.

exit.title: Exit Tsuyo
exit.body: No performance case for this and no price case either. Included for completeness; choosing it would cost $31K and a 12-week transition to replace a supplier meeting every standard except a terms target.

accept.title: Leave terms as they are and log why
accept.body: Logged rationale: "Terms ask deferred to the renewal in April to keep one clean conversation rather than two." Costs nothing today and keeps the $19K on the table for later.

checks.label: Open POs honoured
checks.note: Every transition honours the $412K in flight. No cancellation is used as leverage.

checks.label: Strategic-supplier exit
checks.note: No strategic supplier is being exited.

checks.label: Safety-stock impact accepted
checks.note: $18K of safety stock has to reach Planner before approval.

checks.label: Nothing sent automatically
checks.note: Briefs and messages are drafted in Execute. A person sends them, at every dial setting.

checks.label: Rationale logged
checks.note: Every decision files to LEDGER-SUP-0184 with its should-cost basis.
